item.title: US Department of Labor seeks input from West Virginia highway construction industry to establish prevailing wage rates
item.description: WEST VIRGINIA – The U.S. Department of Labor’s Wage and Hour Division is asking the highway construction industry of West Virginia to participate in a survey to help the agency establish prevailing wage rates, as required under the Davis-Bacon Act and Related Acts, for the payment of construction workers on federally funded and federally assisted construction projects.The survey requests information about wages paid to workers on highway construction projects in West Virginia where construction occurred between Aug. 3, 2025, and Nov. 2, 2026. This is a statewide survey and is not limited to only federally funded construction projects. The data collection period will begin Aug. 3, 2026, and will conclude on Nov. 2, 2026. Participation in the survey process is critical to the publication of prevailing wage and fringe benefit rates that accurately reflect the rates paid in the area being surveyed and the department encourages all stakeholders to participate. The DBRA directs the department to set the prevailing wage rates that reflect the actual wages and fringe benefits paid to construction workers in the county where the work takes place. Complete determinations also reduce the need for contractors to request additional labor classifications. The division will send notification e-mails to interested parties and contractors known to the agency directing participants to the website where they can complete the survey online. All contractors and other interested parties are encouraged to participate in the survey online, regardless of whether they receive an e-mail. Survey participants are asked to please complete and submit the survey by Nov. 2, 2026.If you have questions about the survey process or related forms, please contact the Davis-Bacon Survey Center at 202-343-2005 or DavisBaconInfo@dol.gov. More information about this survey is available via two free online briefings that will describe the survey process and provide instructions for completing the survey. Thes

item.title: US Department of Labor files amicus brief supporting fiduciary discretion in use of forfeited funds under ERISA
item.description: WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of Labor today filed an amicus brief urging the Fourth Circuit to affirm a district court’s decision dismissing the claims in Stana v. SAS Institute Inc., No. 26-1305, that the employer breached its fiduciary obligations by not using forfeited funds for plan expenses.In the amicus brief, the department asserted that the district court appropriately determined the plan fiduciary did not violate its duty of loyalty to plan participants. The plaintiffs’ argument that forfeitures should be allocated to pay plan expenses does not allow for the fact that the plan at issue gave the fiduciary that allocated the forfeitures discretion over them under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act.The department has primary authority to interpret and enforce provisions of Title I of ERISA to ensure fair and impartial administration and compliance with its requirements.The plaintiffs in the case were employed by the SAS Institute and participated in its retirement plan that allowed employees to be fully vested after five years of employment. If a participant left the company before completing five years of employment, the employee would forfeit the balance of the company’s unvested matching contributions. item.content:encoded: WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of Labor today filed an amicus brief urging the Fourth Circuit to affirm a district court’s decision dismissing the claims in Stana v. SAS Institute Inc., No. 26-1305, that the employer breached its fiduciary obligations by not using forfeited funds for plan expenses.In the amicus brief, the department asserted that the district court appropriately determined the plan fiduciary did not violate its duty of loyalty to plan participants. The plaintiffs’ argument that forfeitures should be allocated to pay plan expenses does not allow for the fact that the plan at issue gave the fiduciary that allocated the forfeitures discretion over them under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act.The department has primary authority to interpret and enforce provisions of Title I of ERISA to ensure fair and impartial administration and compliance with its requirements.The plaintiffs in the case were employed by the SAS Institute and participated in its retirement plan that allowed employees to be fully vested after five years of employment. If a participant left the company before completing five years of employment, the employee would forfeit the balance of the company’s unvested matching contributions. As the plan manager, SAS has the power to determine how forfeited funds are distributed, the brief said.Between 2018 and 2023, SAS generally opted to use the forfeited funds to reduce its matching contributions. However, in 2022, SAS chose to allocate $222,320 in forfeitures toward plan expenses. Plaintiffs claimed that unless the plan was on the verge of insolvency, SAS should have used all forfeitures to pay plan expenses to reduce costs for participants.Under ERISA, retirement plan administrators must act loyally. They do not act disloyally by choosing to use forfeitures for employers’ plan contributions rather than plan expenses, the department said. The brief also contended that continued litigation of this type could have the unintended effect of disincentivizing employers from creating retirement plans. Read the department’s amicus brief in Stana v. SAS Institute.

Plaintiff Domah D. Davies (“Davies”) defaulted on his car loan, and Defendant Bangor Federal Credit Union (the “Credit Union”) repossessed and sold the car. In response, Davies filed an Amended Class Action Complaint (the “Amended Complaint ”) against the Credit Union, setting forth two counts. Count I claims that the Credit Union’s repossession notice violates Maine’s Uniform Commercial Code (the “UCC”) . Count II claims that the Credit Union’s deficiency notice violates the UCC. Pursuant to M.R. Civ. P. 12(b)(6), the Credit Union moves to dismiss both counts for failure to state a claim. For the reasons discussed below, the Court grants the Motion to Dismiss with regard to Count I, and denies the Motion with regard to Count II. STANDARD OF REVIEW In reviewing a motion t o dismiss under Rule 12(b)(6), courts “consider the facts in the complaint as if they were admitted.” Bonney v. Stephens Mem. Hosp., 2011 ME 46, ¶ 16, 17 A.3d 123. The complaint is viewed “in the light most favorable to the plaintiff to determine whether i t sets forth elements of a cause of action or alleges facts that would entitle the plaintiff to relief pursuant to some legal theory.” Id. (quoting Saunders v. Tisher, 2006 ME 94, ¶ 8, 902 A.2d 830). “Dismissal is warranted when it appears beyond a doubt t hat the plaintiff is not entitled to relief under any set of facts that he might prove in support of his claim.” Id. 2

DHHS → Office of MaineCare Services (OMS) → Provider Resources → Single Assessment Timing Requirements Reminder

Single Assessment Timing Requirements Reminder

Aug 11, 2026

The summary below outlines the timing requirements for initial and repeat Single Assessments, including the limited exceptions to the standard annual assessment cycle for children receiving medium- and high-intensity behavioral health services.

 

Situation

When is a Single Assessment Required?

Timing

Child already receiving services (no prior Single Assessment)

If the child has never had a Single Assessment, complete one before the next authorization is issued. After that, follow the standard annual reassessment schedule.

Before the next authorization (typically at the next Continued Stay Review (CSR)), then every 12 months

New request for medium- or high-intensity services

Complete a Single Assessment before submitting the initial referral or authorization request.

Initial assessment

Child continues receiving medium- or high-intensity services

Repeat the Single Assessment to confirm ongoing eligibility. Continue submitting CSRs between annual assessments.

Every 12 months

Child residing in a Children’s Residential Care Facility (CRCF)

Complete a Single Assessment when discharge planning begins to determine eligibility for community-based services after discharge.

At discharge planning

On a CRCF wait list

Repeat the Single Assessment while the child remains on the wait list.

Every 6 months

Child receiving services that began before the Single Assessment process was implemented

If no Single Assessment has been completed and the current authorization is nearing expiration, complete an initial Single Assessment before the next authorization. After that, follow the annual reassessment schedule.

At the first CSR after Single Assessment implementation, then every 12 months thereafter.

 

For questions, please contact Karen Sax-McLoughlin, Principal Settlement Manager at the Office of Behavioral Health.

item.content:encoded:
Important Information Regarding Cancellation of Certificate of Title:

Pursuant to Title 29-A, section §669, beginning on July 29, 2026, residents of the state of Maine are able to request cancellation of their Certificate of Title for Tiny Home or Manufactured Home for purposes of obtaining residential real property.


When a Tiny Home or Manufactured Home is permanently affixed to land that you own, or land where you have permission from the land owner via a signed sworn statement, you may request to cancel the Certificate of Title. Once the Certificate of Title is cancelled, the home becomes part of the residential real property instead of being treated as personal property. Under Maine law, this process is handled through the county Registry of Deeds and the Maine Secretary of State Bureau of Motor Vehicles.
 

How to Cancel your Certificate of Tittle for Tiny Home or Manufactured Home 

Before requesting cancellation of the title, make sure:

  • You own the Tiny Home or Manufactured Home and the land where it is located; and/or
  • The individual that owns the property has given a sworn signed statement of authorization.
  • The home has been permanently affixed to the property in accordance with Maine law.
  • Any existing liens have been released or the lienholder has agreed to release the lien upon cancellation of the title.

  • This process is not for double-wide mobile homes/trailers

1. Gather the required documentation

You will need to obtain the following documents before submitting your request:

  • The Original Certificate of Title
  • A description of the home, including;
    • Model Year
    • Manufacturer {make}
    • Width
    • Length
    • Identification Number/Serial Number
  • Lien Release Documentation, if applicable
  • The legal description of the real property
  • A sworn statement confirming:
    • You own both the land, and the Tiny Home or Manufactured Home, or a sworn statement from the property land owner
    • The home is permanently affixed to the property/ground

If you are unable to locate your current Certificate of Title for Tiny Home or Manufactured Home, you are able to request a duplicate title by printing off the Duplicate Title Request Application {MVT-8} and mailing it into our Bureau of Motor Vehicles office with a $33 check-or-moneyorder payable to "Secretary of State". Once a duplicate title is obtained, you wll then be able to continue to the next step.
2. Record the appropriate documents with the Registry of Deeds

Take all the above documents listed to the Registry of Deeds in the county where the property is located. The Registry of Deeds will record the documents as part of the public land records.

For further information on the nearest Registry of Deeds and other contact information, please Maine Registry of Deeds 

3. Submit the Request for Cancellation of Certificate of Title

After the documents above have been recorded, submit a completed MVT-61: Request for Cancellation of Certificate of Title for Tiny Home or Manufactured Housing and provide all original documentation that was recorded within the Registry of Deeds {photocopies are not accepted}. Be sure to include the Book and Page number from the prior step from the Registry of Deeds

4. Receive Confirmation and record Cancellation Letter with Registry of Deeds

Once the Secretary of State reviews and approves your request, you will be mailed a Cancellation Letter stating the process is complete. You must then have the Cancellation Letter document recorded within the county Registry of Deeds. This is a crucial step, as the application process is pending the verification of receipt and recording at the Registry of Deeds office.

5. Return proof of recording to the Bureau of Motor Vehicles

As mentioned above, this process is dependent on the documentation within the public record of the residential real property. Once that document has been recorded within the Registry of Deeds, please return proof of filing with the Bureau of Motor Vehicles via email, both of which are listed below;

Email: titles.bmv@maine.gov

Disclaimer: This information is intended as a general overview of the Maine titling process for Tiny Homes and Manufactured Homes. Requirements may vary depending on the circumstances of the transaction. For further information, please contact the Title Services Division at 207-624-9000 extension 52138, Monday through Friday 08:30AM to 4:30PM
